newsitem.title: CHINA: Coke opens 17th China plant in business boom.
newsitem.headline: Coke opens 17th China plant in business boom.

text.p: Coca-Cola opened its 17th plant in China on Thursday and the head of its China operation said sales this year were expected to grow 32 percent with no end in sight to phenomenonal growth.

The plant, in the central Chinese city of Zhengzhou, will supply Coke to the 90 million people in the province of Henan where consumption levels of Coke average less than two bottles per person per year, compared to 300 for the United States, representing huge growth potential, John Farrell said.
In a telephone interview, he said the $18 million plant was 70 percent owned by a joint venture between Coke, Hong Kong-based Swire Beverages Ltd and China International Trust and Investment Corp.
A 24 percent stake is held by a local Zhengzhou state-owned food factory, with the rest held by Beijing Chong Yin Industrial and Trading Co.
Farrell said total Chinese sales of Coca-Cola in 1996 would be an estimated 230-250 million units, equivalent to six billion bottles of Coke, or five for every person in the country.
Annual growth in sales would this year be around 32 percent, compared to 38 percent for 1995, with similar growth rates expected to be maintained almost indefinitely, he said.
